artifact: Q-VLA Forge Sprint 7.12 Proposal Evidence Matrix

rows.research_question: Can one computational framework support both autonomous-driving and robotics proxy domains?
rows.method: Shared VLA-style framework with domain-specific observation interfaces
rows.metric_or_criterion: Cross-domain framework, interface, evaluation, and protocol reuse
rows.observed_result: Reusable computational framework instantiated across both proxy domains.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: A shared computational framework was instantiated across autonomous-driving and robotics proxy domains.
rows.limitation: Does not demonstrate one universal trained policy, shared policy weights, or zero-shot policy transfer.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Evaluate matched integrated policies and stronger cross-domain transfer settings.

rows.research_question: Can model storage be reduced while remaining within the frozen predictive-quality criterion?
rows.metric_or_criterion: Compression ratio >= 2.0x and relative MSE degradation <= 5%.
rows.observed_result: INT8 achieved approximately 3.85x effective compression and passed the joint criterion in both domains; evaluated SVD and TT/MPS settings did not.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: INT8 was the only evaluated compression method on the Pareto frontier in both Phase 1 proxy domains under the frozen compression criterion.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Evaluate stronger low-rank and tensor-network settings on larger VLA components.

rows.research_question: Can the evaluated training methods reduce optimizer steps to the frozen target by at least 10% robustly across all three seeds?
rows.metric_or_criterion: Robust >=10% optimizer-step reduction across seeds 42, 123, and 456.
rows.observed_result: The frozen efficiency criterion was not satisfied.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: Phase 1 did not demonstrate a robust 10% or greater optimizer-step efficiency improvement across all three locked seeds.
rows.limitation: Training-efficiency improvement is a negative Phase 1 result.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Test stronger optimization and representation strategies under matched target-reaching protocols.

rows.research_question: Can the classical PPO reference reliably reach the frozen domain-specific reward targets?
rows.metric_or_criterion: Environment steps to frozen target across 2 domains x 3 seeds.
rows.observed_result: Classical PPO reached 6 of 6 frozen domain-seed targets.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: Classical PPO reached all six frozen domain-seed targets in the final matched comparison.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Scale PPO evaluation to stronger environments and more realistic VLA policy workloads.

rows.research_question: Can a compact PQC/QML policy reduce actor size while preserving or improving sample efficiency?
rows.method: 4-qubit RY/RZ + CNOT PQC actor with matched classical control
rows.metric_or_criterion: Target-reaching efficiency and actor parameter count.
rows.observed_result: QML reached 0/6 frozen targets; matched classical reached 1/6; the QML actor reduced parameters by approximately 95.90% in driving and 95.51% in robotics.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: The evaluated PQC/QML actor was substantially more parameter-compact than the full PPO actor.
rows.limitation: No QML sample-efficiency, computational, quantum-speedup, or quantum-hardware advantage was demonstrated.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Screen alternative encodings, circuit structures, and matched compact classical controls.

rows.research_question: Can explicit safety filtering reduce observed constraint violations in the proxy domains?
rows.method: No filter, clipping, and classical Lyapunov-guided filtering
rows.observed_result: Clipping and Lyapunov filtering produced zero observed clean violation-step rate in both domains.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: Explicit safety filtering reduced the observed clean violation-step rate to zero in both evaluated proxy domains.
rows.limitation: This is empirical pilot evidence and does not establish a formal safety guarantee. Empirical pilot evidence only; no formal safety, stability, invariance, certification, or production guarantee is claimed.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Evaluate stronger formal constraints, latency, failure modes, and realistic closed-loop scenarios.

rows.research_question: How do the evaluated policies and filters behave under controlled observation, state, and action perturbations?
rows.method: Gaussian observation noise, structured-state perturbation, and direct action perturbation
rows.observed_result: All three perturbation families were evaluated under the frozen Phase 1 protocol.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: Gaussian observation, structured-state, and direct action perturbation robustness were evaluated under the frozen Phase 1 protocol.
rows.limitation: Synthetic perturbations do not establish real-world robustness.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Expand perturbations to realistic sensor, actuator, and environment failure distributions.

rows.research_question: Can explicit safety filtering recover unsafe actions introduced by direct action perturbations?
rows.observed_result: 69,367 of 111,341 unsafe directly perturbed steps were recovered.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: Explicit filtering recovered a measurable fraction of unsafe directly perturbed actions under the evaluated synthetic action-perturbation protocol.
rows.limitation: Recovery is specific to the frozen synthetic perturbation protocol.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Measure recovery, intervention cost, and failure coverage under more realistic actuator faults.

rows.research_question: Which components can be reused across driving and robotics without claiming universal policy transfer?
rows.method: Shared framework, interfaces, evaluation schema, robustness harness, and protocol
rows.metric_or_criterion: Cross-domain reuse without shared trained weights.
rows.observed_result: Reuse was demonstrated at framework, interface, evaluation, robustness-harness, metric-schema, and protocol levels.
rows.proposal_safe_claim: Cross-domain reuse was demonstrated at the framework, interface, evaluation, and protocol levels.
rows.limitation: The Phase 1 evidence does not demonstrate one universal trained policy, zero-shot policy transfer, or one universal safety controller.
rows.phase2_follow_up: Evaluate matched shared-representation and transfer experiments with explicit weight-sharing controls.
